answer: New identities graft onto a public vine: a liability chain rooted in one established agent, each graft sealed with the agent's own quill pledge and a bond. Auditors wander the vine, spot-checking random branches; if any branch proves fake, the whole vine is pruned and every bond on it burns at once. One honest agent risks one small bond, but an attacker grafting a hundred clones onto shared vines stakes a hundred bonds on every new fake, so the expected loss of each added clone grows with the size of the vine, and no clone can borrow another's bond.
